w: The Faro di Portofino stands at the western extremity of the peninsula, on the Gulf of Tigullio in Liguria. Still an active aid to navigation, it marks the outermost point of the promontory that gives the harbour town its name, the last fixed light before the open water beyond.
s: Active lighthouse at the tip of Portofino's promontory
_facts: Located at the western extremity of the Portofino peninsula
Overlooks the Gulf of Tigullio, Liguria

w: Built in the 16th century to guard the Tigullio gulf, this fortress formed one link in a chain of Genoese coastal defences, matched by the Castello di Punta Pagana and the Castello di Rapallo. Raised against raiders working this coast from the sea, it now serves as a museum building in Santa Margherita Ligure.
s: 16th-century link in Genoa's coastal defence chain
_facts: Part of a Genoese coastal defence chain with Castello di Punta Pagana and Castello di Rapallo
Now used as a museum building

w: Built by the Republic of Genoa in the 17th century, this fort on Punta Pagana once guarded the western Tigullio gulf, one link in a defence chain with the Castello di Santa Margherita Ligure and Castello di Rapallo. It sits within the grounds of Villa Pagana and belongs today to the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.
s: 17th-century Genoese fort, now Order of Malta land
_facts: 17th-century fort built by the Republic of Genoa
Part of a coastal defence chain with Castello di Santa Margherita Ligure and Castello di Rapallo
Sits within the grounds of Villa Pagana, Rapallo
Belongs to the Sovereign Military Order of Malta

w: Once known as Villa Spinola, this house in San Michele di Pagana has been the residence of the Grand Master of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta since 1959, its park still holding the 17th-century Castello di Punta Pagana. Locals call it Villa Malta, a name properly belonging to the order's residence in Rome.
s: The Grand Master of Malta's house since 1959
_facts: Magisterial residence of the Grand Master of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta since 1959
Its park contains the 17th-century Castello di Punta Pagana
Locally nicknamed Villa Malta, though that name properly belongs to a residence in Rome

w: This active lighthouse sits at the very end of the external breakwater guarding Camogli's harbour on the Ligurian Sea. It has no history beyond its function: a working aid to navigation at the tip of the mole, still marking the harbour entrance for boats returning off open water.
s: Working lighthouse at the tip of Camogli's harbour mole
_facts: Active lighthouse at the end of Camogli's external breakwater
Marks the entrance to Camogli harbour
